edition.title: The Daily Signal
edition.kicker: Primary-source tech intelligence, compiled from the live wire.

stories.title: Liquid: patched bridge nodes, coordinated federation restart in the works after ~4,000 BTC white-hat drain
stories.summary: Blockstream's @Blockstream post (2026-09-08 01:00 UTC) is the operator's technical follow-up to the Liquid incident: patched bridge-node software is deployed, the federation is preparing a coordinated restart, and further hardening is promised. The status page confirms the sidechain is still paused - bridge nodes disabled, L-BTC peg-in/out frozen - with USDT/DePix/RWAs reported unaffected. This is the restart phase of the story that topped yesterday's edition; the ~598.5 BTC 'bounty' the white hats kept after returning 3,400 BTC has not been reconciled, and Blockstream has not confirmed 1:1 L-BTC backing or a restart time.

quality.note: Official operator post plus the operator's live status page (fetched in-window: 'September 7, 12:14 AM Active', bridge nodes disabled). Distinct from yesterday's pause story (different canonical URL and event). Restart timing and L-BTC backing state are not yet confirmed.

stories.title: Stacks Genesis Bond enrollment opens in 3 days; anchors UTXO (Nakamoto), HashKey Cloud, 21shares
stories.summary: @Stacks (2026-09-07 20:04 UTC) opened the enrollment runway for the self-custodial Genesis Bond - the permissionless Bitcoin-staking path that the pooled Xverse launch on 09-07 was only the first rung of. Named anchors: UTXO (Nakamoto Inc.), HashKey Cloud, 21shares. Yield is ~3% BTC APY annualized over a Bitcoin year (a single 6-month bond delivers ~1.44%) per Stacks' own docs; the enrollment cap can close before Sep 9. This is the consumer entry point to Stacks' Bitcoin-yield roadmap - still Stacks L2 PoX-5 mechanics, not native Bitcoin L1 consensus staking.

quality.note: Official @Stacks post; canonical product page fetched in-window (target ~3% BTC APY annualized, 6-month bond delivers ~1.44%). Distinct event from yesterday's pooled Xverse launch and the sBTC signers post.

stories.title: DBS and Citi settle a weekend USD payment in minutes on Swift's Digital Ledger (tokenized deposits)
stories.summary: DBS (Singapore) and Citi (New York) completed a weekend cross-border USD payment on Swift's blockchain Digital Ledger using tokenized deposits - settling in minutes instead of up to two business days. It is the second confirmed live use of the ledger that launched in July with 17 banks, following HSBC/Standard Chartered's first cross-border transfer in August. For builders this is the incumbent settlement network shipping 24/7 tokenized-deposit rails that directly compete with stablecoin and Bitcoin-based settlement for corporate liquidity; Swift's 1.5-quadrillion-dollar network is racing to prove it can adapt to always-on settlement.

quality.note: Official bank announcement covered by CoinDesk with in-window @CoinDesk post. Bank rails (tokenized deposits on Swift's ledger), not Bitcoin L1 - included as the incumbent-settlement counterpoint.

stories.title: Malone Lam to plead guilty in ~4,100 BTC / $240M social-engineering Bitcoin theft
stories.summary: The 22-year-old Singaporean at the center of one of the largest cryptocurrency thefts in U.S. history - a ~4,100 BTC (~$240M) social-engineering heist that impersonated Google/Gemini contacts to dupe a stranger into signing transactions - is set to plead guilty in Washington this week per the AP/US News wire (Sept 7). The superseding indictment and upcoming plea hearing cap the criminal phase of the 2024 incident that reshaped how exchanges and wallets treat 'signed-by-victim' outflows. Caveat: the plea is scheduled, not yet entered; co-defendants' outcomes are still pending.

quality.note: AP wire via US News (Sept 7, 07:53 a.m. ET) with in-window @CoinDesk post. Plea hearing reported as scheduled for ~Sept 9, not yet held.

stories.title: sBTC signer set widens with The Tie, Ankr and HashKey Cloud - federation rails around Stacks' BTC-collateral asset
stories.summary: @Stacks added three more institutions - The Tie, Ankr and HashKey Cloud - to the sBTC signer set, the threshold federation that pegs BTC in and out of Stacks' Bitcoin-collateralized asset; HashKey Cloud is also a Genesis Bond launch partner. It is incremental institutional width, not protocol consensus: the signer set remains a threshold federation, and Ankr was already announced 24 Aug so part of this post is a bundled recap. Caveat: yield and capacity numbers in Stacks' docs are self-reported and not independently audited.

quality.note: Official @Stacks post; one signer (Ankr) predates the post, so treat as expansion/recap rather than three same-day joins.

stories.title: Jensen Huang: GPT-6 Astra trained on ~100K+ Grace Blackwell NVLink72, '400K GPUs coming online', 'AGI has arrived'
stories.summary: NVIDIA's @JensenHuang (2026-09-06 20:41 UTC) put out a three-claim infrastructure post tied to OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra: the flagship was trained on ~100K+ NVIDIA Grace Blackwell NVLink72 racks, '400K GPUs coming online next', and 'AGI has arrived'. For builders the load-bearing number is the 100K+ NVL72 figure - a concrete datapoint on frontier-training scale - but all three claims are CEO assertions, not an NVIDIA blog, SKU or benchmark; '400K GPUs' does not specify which cluster or generation, and 'AGI has arrived' is a rhetorical claim, not a product launch. @nvidia itself posted nothing in-window.

quality.note: CEO post only (no NVIDIA blog or system-card URL in the post). GPU counts and the AGI framing are assertions; GPT-6 Astra itself was already covered in the 09-05 edition.

stories.title: ChatGPT Work now learns your writing style from connected Gmail, Drive, Slack and SharePoint
stories.summary: @ChatGPT (2026-09-07 17:44 UTC) shipped a writing-style personalization pass in ChatGPT Work: connect Gmail, Google Drive, Slack and SharePoint and the assistant profiles your tone, formatting and voice for work-facing drafts. It is a workflow feature, not a model - web only, on paid plans with ChatGPT Work - but it is one of the first mainstream agent products to treat 'style transfer from your own corpus' as a first-class setup step. Caveat: the official setup URL is a login callback, not a docs page; the linked blog/release page is thin.

quality.note: Official product-account post; the linked setup URL is the in-product flow, not a docs/blog page. Feature, not a model or API.

stories.title: CoreWeave: BYO-weights 'Dedicated Inference' for Moonshot Kimi K3 (2.8T params, 1M context)
stories.summary: @CoreWeave (2026-09-07 12:37 UTC) promoted its Dedicated Inference path for Moonshot's Kimi K3 - a 2.8T-parameter, 1M-context model - with BYO-weights, autoscaling and routing on NVIDIA GPUs. The canonical how-to blog was actually published 2026-09-03 (datePublished in the page's own schema), so this is an in-window promotional push of an already-shipped capability, not a same-day launch. For builders the signal is that 2.8T MoE-class open models are now a first-class SKU on dedicated GPU clouds rather than just serverless; Kimi K3 weights launched in July, and CoreWeave does not supply or license the model itself.

quality.note: Official @CoreWeave post in-window; the blog's own datePublished is 2026-09-03T15:55:01Z, so the underlying capability predates the post. The tweet itself had no link.

stories.title: Together Compute: GLM-5.3 Flash vs GPT-5.6 Terra on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index - '82% less per task'
stories.summary: @TogetherCompute (2026-09-07 18:38 UTC) published a benchmark-marketing post comparing GLM-5.3 Flash against GPT-5.6 Terra on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, claiming '82% less per task'. GLM-5.3-Flash itself landed on Together's serverless on 2026-08-27, so this is an in-window benchmark push, not a new model - but it is a useful datapoint on how far open-weights GLM-class models have closed the per-task cost gap against frontier proprietary tiers. Caveat: the numbers are vendor-published and the 'Intelligence Index' is one of several agentic benchmarks, not a consensus eval.

quality.note: Vendor-published benchmark post (no independent replication). Model itself launched 2026-08-27 per the changelog; the 09-07 post is the in-window benchmark push.

stories.title: XPENG commissions the world's first automated production line for advanced general-purpose humanoids - first IRON walks off the line on its own
stories.summary: XPENG (2026-09-08, PRNewswire + @XPENG_Global + CEO @xiaopenghexpeng) officially commissioned its Guangzhou humanoid production line and claims the first advanced general-purpose humanoid - IRON - completed automated production and walked off the line on its own. Core-process automation is >80% and the line is built to automotive-grade quality standards; the framing is 'lab to line, 0 to 1'. What they did NOT announce: factory location, annual capacity, takt time, price, ship date or customer orders - so treat it as a production-line commissioning, not mass production. CEO's added claim: 'using robots to mass-produce robots, autonomously.' Commercial deliveries remain guided to 2027.

quality.note: Official PRNewswire release (09-07 22:26 ET) with in-window @XPENG_Global posts. Commissioning claim is vendor-reported; no independent verification of 'world's first' or of autonomous off-line walking.

stories.title: NEURA Robotics and SECO to put humanoid 4NE1 into series production in Europe - Qualcomm Dragonwing Smart Limbs
stories.summary: @NEURARobotics (2026-09-07 09:06 UTC) and @SECO_spa (06:01 UTC, with the partner PR page) announced a series-production partnership: SECO will build the compute modules for NEURA's humanoid 4NE1 and 'Smart Limbs', which run on Qualcomm Dragonwing, with a focus on industrial data and automation for semiconductor and electronics manufacturing. For builders this is one of the more concrete European industrialization deals of the window - a specific compute-module supplier, a specific chip (Dragonwing), and a specific end-market (semis/electronics) - rather than a generic 'we're scaling physical AI' press release. Caveat: it is a partnership, not a shipped product or a funded round; no volume, price or ship date was announced.

quality.note: Two official accounts posted the same-day announcement; partner PR page fetched in-window. Date-only (noon UTC used). Partnership, not a shipped product or funding round.

stories.title: Galbot RoboGesture (ECCV 2026): real-time semantic-aligned co-speech gestures for humanoids on a Unitree G1
stories.summary: Galbot Robotics posted its ECCV 2026 paper RoboGesture (arXiv 2608.28693, project page robogesture.github.io) - a ~2-second listen → respond → gesture loop for humanoid interaction, demonstrated on a Unitree G1. The contribution is the semantic alignment between speech content and co-speech gesture timing, not a new actuator or model family. Poster session is 10 Sep 16:30-18:30 CEST at ECCV (ExHall #178). Caveat: it is a capability demo with a project page, not a commercial product or a funded round; the 'real-time' claim is vendor-reported and the demo hardware is a third-party (Unitree) platform.

quality.note: Official company post plus arXiv paper and project page, all fetched in-window. 72h catch-up edge (09-05 18:52 UTC). Capability demo, not a commercial deployment.

stories.title: Agility Robotics' S-4 (2026-09-04): 'substantial doubt' about continuing as a going concern without the Churchill XI merger
stories.summary: Agility Robotics' (CCXI-merger partner) S-4 registration statement, filed 2026-09-04 with the SEC, states that without consideration of the proposed Churchill Capital XI business combination, Agility 'has concluded there is substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern.' The filing notes operating losses since inception, expected continuation of negative cash flows, and that the auditor (Grant Thornton) concurred on the going-concern assessment for FY2025. This is the first time the going-concern language has been visible in a public SEC filing for Agility - a data point that the humanoid sector's capital intensity is outpacing even well-customered operators, and that the SPAC close is load-bearing for continuity. Caveat: it is an S-4 risk-factor disclosure, not a 10-K; the merger is still subject to shareholder and regulatory approval.

source.name: SEC EDGAR - Agility Robotics / Churchill Capital XI S-4

quality.note: Direct SEC EDGAR filing (fetched in-window; 30 going-concern hits, auditor-concurred language confirmed). Date-only, noon UTC used. 72h catch-up edge (filed 09-04). S-4, not 10-K; merger still pending.

stories.title: ABB PixelPaint now in production at Mercedes-Benz Sindelfingen - first on the Maybach SL 680 Monogram Series
stories.summary: @ABBRobotics (2026-09-07 14:23 UTC) announced that its PixelPaint automotive-painting system is now running in production at Mercedes-Benz's Sindelfingen plant, with the Mercedes-Maybach SL 680 Monogram Series as the first model finished with it. It is a live industrial deployment of an existing ABB painting system (not a new robot platform), but it is a notable 'first' for a named, premium model and a concrete data point on how much of the paint-shop step has moved to robotic, pixel-level finishing. Caveat: deployment announcement, not a new SKU or a funded round; no throughput or cost numbers were published.

quality.note: Official @ABBRobotics post only (no ABB blog URL linked in the post). Deployment of an existing system, not a new platform.

stories.title: Insilico Medicine: six proteomic aging clocks all predict younger in the rentosertib Phase 2a IPF trial - peak ~3-4 year predicted-age drop at week 4
stories.summary: Zhavoronkov et al. (Nature Biotechnology, published 2026-09-07; @InSilicoMeds and @NatureBiotech posted the paper in-window) used 12-week longitudinal Olink proteomic data (CNCB OMIX008341, n=42) from the published Phase 2a IPF trial of rentosertib - an AI-designed TNIK inhibitor - and found that six independently developed proteomic aging clocks (ProtAge, OrganAge, PAC, ipfP3GPT, PAOPAC, etc.) consistently predicted lower biological age in the treated arms, peaking at ~3-4 years younger at week 4 (30 mg BID), with one clock showing up to ~6 years. The authors frame it as a dual-purpose trial blueprint for embedding geroscience endpoints into standard disease trials, aligned with FDA Biomarker/BEST. Caveats the authors state: n is small, all patients have IPF, and the study cannot yet separate geroprotection from treating the lung; rentosertib is already in Phase 3 in China for IPF - this paper is not a new trial launch. No medical advice.

quality.note: Peer-reviewed Nature Biotechnology paper (fetched in-window) with the company's official X post, the journal's official post, and the first author's personal post all in-window. Human clinical (Phase 2a) data, not animal or observational; the 'aging reversal' framing is the authors'/company's, and Levitt's caveat is that it cannot yet separate geroprotection from lung treatment.

stories.title: Cell: skin-innervating glutamatergic neurons modulate aging - sensory innervation of skin as an aging regulator
stories.summary: Cell Press posted a new Cell paper (S0092-8674(26)00752-X, @CellCellPress 2026-09-06 23:08 UTC) showing that skin-innervating glutamatergic neurons modulate aging - a result that puts the sensory nervous system's skin projection on the list of aging regulators, alongside the more-cited metabolic and immune pathways. It is basic geroscience (mechanism, not intervention), and the in-window event is the journal's issue publication and official post. No medical advice; no drug or dose is implied.

quality.note: Official Cell Press post plus the Cell abstract page, both fetched in-window. Basic mechanism paper, not an intervention study.

stories.title: Science: two prophylactic psilocybin doses prevented CIPN in mice across chemo cycles without blunting the antitumor effect
stories.summary: Heles et al. (Science, published 2026-09-03; @ScienceMagazine and @Nature amplified in-window on 09-07) showed that two doses of psilocybin given before each of six chemotherapy cycles over eight months completely prevented mice from developing chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) - a condition that affects up to 60% of people on platinum-based regimens - without reducing the chemotherapy's tumor-shrinking effect. The mechanism is preservation of mitochondrial trafficking into distal sensory neurons, not a classic analgesic effect. For builders this is a 'prevent the damage, not treat the pain' design pattern with a specific, checkable molecular target; for the aging/healthspan space it is a direct data point on neuroprotection in an age-relevant indication. Caveat: mouse/human-tissue data, not a human trial - the authors say human trials are starting, not yet reported. No medical advice.

quality.note: Peer-reviewed Science paper (DOI verified via Crossref, published 2026-09-03) with in-window @ScienceMagazine and @Nature amplification. Mouse/human-tissue data, not a human trial; 'Catch-up' edge - the paper predates the 30h window but the journal amplification and community reaction are the in-window event.

stories.title: Bill Ackman's daughter received a first-of-its-kind FDA-emergency-authorized mitochondrial transplant from leg to eyes
stories.summary: The Washington Post (2026-09-06) reports that Bill Ackman's 26-year-old daughter Lucy, who lost sight after a brain hemorrhage crushed her optic nerve, received an experimental mitochondrial transplant - mitochondria moved from her leg muscle to her eyes - under a one-time FDA emergency authorization granted in May 2026. It is the most prominent human use yet of the 'mitochondrial transplant for neural repair' strategy, which is of direct interest to longevity researchers because mitochondria are a recurring target in aging research (the 2024 Nature mouse optic-nerve paper is the precedent). It is a single-patient case report, not a trial or an approval; the team is hoping for optic-nerve healing and possible partial vision restoration. No medical advice.

quality.note: WaPo original (09-06) with independent Yahoo/Benzinga coverage, all fetched in-window. Single-patient case report, not a trial; the FDA authorization was a one-time emergency use, not a standing approval.
